deviations.what: The location columns are added by a mixin when the resource is built, and the point is set through LocationField.compress, rather than by two import-export fields that each set the point.
deviations.why: The field list of a registered type is only known when the factory runs, and compress carries every rule and message of the form, so a refused row is reported with the form's wording.

concerns: fairdm/registry/factories.py ResourceFactory._get_fk_widgets: a foreign key to a model with natural_key gets ForeignKeyWidget(model, "natural_key"), which names no field, and Dataset's default manager hides private datasets from the widget's lookup. A generated resource's dataset column therefore cannot import against a private dataset or by dataset uuid. The tests declare the dataset column themselves with a primary-key widget on a public dataset. Not changed here (outside US5); import views are not routed (R21), so nothing meets it today.
A generated resource does not attribute rows to the dataset it was constructed with (BaseFairDMResource.before_import_row does); a row needs its dataset column. Same area, left alone.

An elevation or uncertainty cell that is not a number is reported as an invalid row with float's own message (could not convert string to float), not the location input's wording. The row is not saved. The input's form says 'Enter a number', so a shared message could be chosen when R21 routes import.

The three tests for empty cells, an elevation-only file and the hand-written resources' measurement case were written after the code as characterisations of behaviour locations.md states; the hand-written sample case and the others were red first.
